claims.title: Battle of Hafrsfjord
claims.summary: Harald Fairhair defeated a coalition of petty kings from the south-west at Hafrsfjord, the decisive victory by which tradition holds he became the first king over all of Norway.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-872-battle-of-hafrsfjord, claim TL:NOR:event:872:battle-of-hafrsfjord, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Control of the coastal trade routes
claims.summary: From his base at Avaldsnes on Karmøy, Harald Fairhair dominated the coastal sailing route that linked northern Norway with the markets of Kaupang and Hedeby, anchoring royal power in trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-900-control-of-the-coastal-trade-routes, claim TL:NOR:event:900:control-of-the-coastal-trade-routes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Harald Fairhair and fragmentation
claims.summary: On Harald's death his realm broke apart among his sons, beginning decades of dynastic conflict, though the idea of a single Norwegian kingship endured.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-930-death-of-harald-fairhair-and-fragmentation, claim TL:NOR:event:930:death-of-harald-fairhair-and-fragmentation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conventional close of the Viking Age
claims.summary: The era of large-scale Scandinavian raiding is conventionally closed in 1066, by which time Norway was a Christianising kingdom rather than a society of independent sea-kings.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1066-conventional-close-of-the-viking-age, claim TL:NOR:event:1066:conventional-close-of-the-viking-age, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Moster assembly and Christian law
claims.summary: Olaf II established a nationwide church organisation and Christian law at Moster, banning non-Christian worship and making Christianity the kingdom's only permitted religion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1024-moster-assembly-and-christian-law, claim TL:NOR:event:1024:moster-assembly-and-christian-law, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Stiklestad and the death of St Olaf
claims.summary: King Olaf II was killed at Stiklestad. Declared holy within a year and enshrined at Nidaros, he became Norway's patron saint and eternal king, accelerating the Christianisation of the realm.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1030-battle-of-stiklestad-and-the-death-of-st-olaf, claim TL:NOR:event:1030:battle-of-stiklestad-and-the-death-of-st-olaf, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The national law of Magnus the Lawmender
claims.summary: King Magnus VI codified a national law for the whole kingdom, one of the most advanced legal codes in medieval Europe and a mark of the consolidated Christian monarchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1274-the-national-law-of-magnus-the-lawmender, claim TL:NOR:event:1274:the-national-law-of-magnus-the-lawmender, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Hanseatic Kontor at Bryggen
claims.summary: German merchants of the Hanseatic League established their trading office at Bryggen in Bergen, which became Norway's foremost town and a hub of northern commerce for some four centuries, until 1754.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1350-the-hanseatic-kontor-at-bryggen, claim TL:NOR:event:1350:the-hanseatic-kontor-at-bryggen, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Black Death reaches Norway
claims.summary: Plague arrived by ship at Bergen and spread through the country, killing about half the population and devastating the native aristocracy and clergy, a turning point in Norwegian history.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1349-the-black-death-reaches-norway, claim TL:NOR:event:1349:the-black-death-reaches-norway, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kalmar Union
claims.summary: Under Queen Margaret I of Denmark, Denmark, Norway and Sweden were united in the Kalmar Union, with Erik of Pomerania crowned common king; Norway became the weakest of the three partners.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1397-the-kalmar-union, claim TL:NOR:event:1397:the-kalmar-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Norway reduced to a Danish province
claims.summary: After Sweden left the union, Norway remained tied to Denmark and was governed from Copenhagen, becoming in effect a Danish province while keeping its own laws and church.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1537-norway-reduced-to-a-danish-province, claim TL:NOR:event:1537:norway-reduced-to-a-danish-province, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Treaty of Kiel
claims.summary: Defeated in the Napoleonic Wars, Denmark-Norway was forced to cede Norway: by the Treaty of Kiel the Danish king renounced all claims to Norway in favour of the king of Sweden.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1814-the-treaty-of-kiel, claim TL:NOR:event:1814:the-treaty-of-kiel, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Constitution of Eidsvoll
claims.summary: A constituent assembly at Eidsvoll signed Norway's constitution on 17 May 1814, declaring the country a free kingdom with an elected Storting; the date became the national day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1814-the-constitution-of-eidsvoll, claim TL:NOR:event:1814:the-constitution-of-eidsvoll, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union with Sweden
claims.summary: After a short war, Sweden accepted the Eidsvoll constitution and the Storting voted to enter a personal union with Sweden under a shared king, with Norway keeping its parliament and laws.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1814-union-with-sweden, claim TL:NOR:event:1814:union-with-sweden, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Romantic nationalism and a national culture
claims.summary: A movement of romantic nationalism drew on Norwegian history, landscape and folk tradition; Ibsen, Grieg and Munch gave the nation a place in world culture and reinforced a separate identity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1864-romantic-nationalism-and-a-national-culture, claim TL:NOR:event:1864:romantic-nationalism-and-a-national-culture, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Parliamentarism and the consular dispute
claims.summary: The introduction of parliamentary government strengthened the Storting, while the conflict with Sweden over Norway's right to its own consular service drove the two countries apart.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1884-parliamentarism-and-the-consular-dispute, claim TL:NOR:event:1884:parliamentarism-and-the-consular-dispute, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dissolution of the union with Sweden
claims.summary: The Storting declared the union with Sweden dissolved; confirmed by referendum and settled peacefully at Karlstad, it made Norway a fully sovereign state for the first time in centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1905-dissolution-of-the-union-with-sweden, claim TL:NOR:event:1905:dissolution-of-the-union-with-sweden, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Election of King Haakon VII
claims.summary: After a plebiscite to retain a monarchy, the Storting elected Prince Carl of Denmark as king; he took the name Haakon VII, founding the modern Norwegian royal house.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1905-election-of-king-haakon-vii, claim TL:NOR:event:1905:election-of-king-haakon-vii, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Svalbard (Spitsbergen) Treaty
claims.summary: Signed in Paris, the treaty recognised Norwegian sovereignty over Svalbard while granting all signatories equal rights to economic activity and barring warlike use; Norway took over administration in 1925.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1920-the-svalbard-spitsbergen-treaty, claim TL:NOR:event:1920:the-svalbard-spitsbergen-treaty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Eastern Greenland case
claims.summary: The Permanent Court of International Justice ruled against Norway's claim to part of eastern Greenland, upholding Danish sovereignty over the whole island; Norway abandoned its claim.

sources.label: Legal Status of Eastern Greenland (Denmark v. Norway), 1933

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1933-eastern-greenland-case, claim TL:NOR:event:1933:eastern-greenland-case, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: German invasion and the Quisling regime
claims.summary: Germany invaded on 9 April 1940; the king and government went into exile while Vidkun Quisling proclaimed a government, beginning five years of occupation and collaboration.

sources.label: Vidkun Quisling's illegal government in Oslo 1940

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1940-german-invasion-and-the-quisling-regime, claim TL:NOR:event:1940:german-invasion-and-the-quisling-regime, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Norway joins NATO
claims.summary: Abandoning prewar neutrality, Norway became a founding member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, anchoring its security in the Western alliance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1949-norway-joins-nato, claim TL:NOR:event:1949:norway-joins-nato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Oil discovered at Ekofisk
claims.summary: Phillips Petroleum struck oil at the Ekofisk field in the North Sea, confirmed on Christmas Eve 1969; the discovery transformed Norway into a wealthy petroleum state with a vast sovereign wealth fund.

sources.label: The discovery which changed Norway – Ekofisk

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1969-oil-discovered-at-ekofisk, claim TL:NOR:event:1969:oil-discovered-at-ekofisk, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First referendum rejects the European Community
claims.summary: A majority of 53.5 per cent of Norwegians voted against joining the European Community, keeping the country outside the integration process.

sources.label: Norway and the EU: Historical overview
sources.publisher: Mission of Norway to the EU (norway.no)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1972-first-referendum-rejects-the-european-community, claim TL:NOR:event:1972:first-referendum-rejects-the-european-community, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second referendum rejects the European Union
claims.summary: A majority of 52.2 per cent again rejected membership, this time of the European Union; Norway remained outside the EU while joining its single market through the EEA.

sources.label: Norway and the EU: Historical overview
sources.publisher: Mission of Norway to the EU (norway.no)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Norway: From the Viking kingdoms and a saint-king to North Sea oil, Arctic sovereignty and a prosperous modern realm.", terralore.co/country/NOR/chronicle#ev-1994-second-referendum-rejects-the-european-union, claim TL:NOR:event:1994:second-referendum-rejects-the-european-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Barents Sea delimitation treaty with Russia
claims.summary: Norway and Russia signed a treaty dividing the disputed 175,000 sq km of the Barents Sea and Arctic Ocean, ending a roughly forty-year dispute; in force from 2011, it replaced the Grey Zone arrangement.

sources.label: Agreement reached between Norway and the Russian Federation in the negotiations on maritime delimitation

Norway and Russia Agree on Maritime Boundary in the Barents Sea and the Arctic Ocean
sources.publisher: American Society of International Law (ASIL Insights)
